title: Unable to use a stylus to switch to a workspace by touching it to an area with a window
line: Tapping a window in the Pager with a pen or finger now switches to that desktop instead of grabbing the window.
explanation: The Pager's window outlines use drag.threshold: 1, so a window drag starts as soon as the pointer moves a single pixel during a press. That was done on purpose for bug 460541, so windows can still be dragged with a mouse in small pagers, but a pen tap always wobbles a few pixels, so it grabbed the window and the release never switched desktop. The change adds a passive PointHandler for pens and touchscreens: while one of them is pressed, the outline uses the platform's start drag distance, and mouse presses keep the 1 px threshold.

commits.message:
applets/pager: Don't grab windows on wobbly pen and touch taps

Window outlines start a drag after one pixel so small pagers still allow
dragging, but pen and finger taps always wobble a bit, so they grabbed
the window. Give pen and touch presses the platform start drag distance.

BUG: 513474

patches.diff:
From a0c44205ffc4c8399c91aed9031afdddebae4e0c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:03:14 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/pager: Don't grab windows on wobbly pen and touch
 taps

Window outlines start a drag after one pixel so small pagers still allow
dragging, but pen and finger taps always wobble a bit, so they grabbed
the window. Give pen and touch presses the platform start drag distance.

BUG: 513474
---
 applets/pager/qml/main.qml | 9 ++++++++-
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/pager/qml/main.qml b/applets/pager/qml/main.qml
index b4211ddbbd..98b43503af 100644
--- a/applets/pager/qml/main.qml
+++ b/applets/pager/qml/main.qml
@@ -523,8 +523,15 @@ PlasmoidItem {
                                 id: windowMouseArea
                                 anchors.fill: parent
 
+                                // A mouse needs a tiny threshold in small pagers, but pen and finger taps
+                                // always wobble a little and must not grab the window.
+                                PointHandler {
+                                    id: tapWobbleHandler
+                                    acceptedDevices: PointerDevice.TouchScreen | PointerDevice.Stylus
+                                }
+
                                 drag.target: windowRect
-                                drag.threshold: 1
+                                drag.threshold: tapWobbleHandler.active ? Application.styleHints.startDragDistance : 1
                                 drag.axis: Drag.XAndYAxis
                                 drag.minimumX: 0
                                 drag.maximumX: root.width - windowRect.width
--

reviews.text: Well-scoped QML fix that solves wobbly stylus and touch taps grabbing window outlines in the Pager without regressing the 1 px mouse drag threshold needed for small pagers (bug 460541). Using a passive PointHandler for TouchScreen and Stylus to switch drag.threshold to Application.styleHints.startDragDistance is idiomatic, avoids interfering with MouseArea grabs, and is cleanly verified for both wobbly taps and intentional drags.

Correct cause: the window outline's drag.threshold: 1 turns any pen wobble into a window drag, so onReleased never forwards the click to the desktop. The fix keeps the 1 px threshold for mice (bug 460541) and gives pen/touch presses the platform start drag distance through a passive PointHandler, a clean device split that Plasma already uses elsewhere; a tap then switches desktop and a deliberate pen drag still moves the window, which meets the reporter's goal (they suggested press-and-hold, but a distance threshold is the standard Plasma behavior). Injected tablet events on the rig and the before/after media show the switch, the pen drag and the unchanged mouse drag. Touch dragging was only checked in a standalone scene, as the notes honestly say; worth a quick real-touch check but not blocking.
